gen-gf-happy-monkey-fs-gambetta: Happy Monkey draws every line like ruler-straight wire, gaps wide in the e. Gambetta, a text serif, does the opposite job, letting its stroke weight swell and ease across a paragraph.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-lora: Lora reads literary and settled, its hairline thinning at the curves barely noticeable. And Happy Monkey glides above it like wire, bold and straight, so the two feel nothing alike.
gen-gf-phudu-fs-gambetta: Bookish and graceful, Gambetta lets its stroke weight shift gently, never dramatically, through wide channels into each counter. But Phudu above it keeps a steady, unvarying line, like a ballpoint, so the two feel quite different.
gen-gf-phudu-lora: Bent tubing, basically: Phudu's letters curve with generous openings. Lora then follows with a friendly, mild contrast in the stroke, and a longer paragraph would move along comfortably.
gen-gf-pixelify-sans-fs-gambetta: Pixelify Sans has a c as open as a bent paperclip. Gambetta follows with a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight, so a long paragraph moves along gracefully.
gen-gf-pixelify-sans-lora: Lora reads literary, with modest hairline thinning at the curves and a broad, welcoming c. Lora can sit modestly below Pixelify Sans, whose cable-bent letters never swell or thin, if the heading is given more size.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-fs-gambetta: Shantell Sans looks drawn with one fixed pen tip, mouth wide open. Its strength is that single-nib directness, while Gambetta's barely tilted calligraphy nib does the quieter work of carrying text.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-lora: Lora brings a literary voice, its serif strokes shifting mildly like a pen's, with a broad, welcoming c. Shantell Sans, bent-paperclip simple, is the loud one.
gen-gf-sniglet-fs-gambetta: Sniglet's horizontal bars are as heavy as its upright stems. Gambetta, a serif with a mild thick-and-thin rhythm, would read in a gracious, bookish way across a longer passage.
gen-gf-sniglet-lora: Lora, a serif with gentle stroke weight variation, sits under Sniglet's pipe-bodied, level-beat letters. A longer passage would feel literary and easy.
